# Finish and deliver the result {.unnumbered}

The analysis may be settled, but what does the figure need before a manuscript,
poster, or slide audience can use it? These recipes choose the visual finish
first, then combine, annotate, size, and export the result for the reader who
receives it.

## Choose the next recipe

| Your question | Recipe | Why this one |
|---|---|---|
| Which house style should the finished figure use? | [Themes for consistency](themes.qmd) | Applies the manuscript, poster, or presentation theme. |
| How do I use the house palette consistently? | [Color templates for consistency](colors.qmd) | Keeps categorical and continuous colors aligned across figures. |
| How do I label the clinical details a reader needs? | [Annotating figures and formatting axes](annotation.qmd) | Adds annotations and readable axis formatting. |
| When does the figure need a legend and how should it read? | [Using legends](legends.qmd) | Builds legends that explain the visual encoding without taking over the plot. |
| How do I arrange several panels into one figure? | [Combination figures](combination.qmd) | Combines plots into a manuscript-ready layout. |
| Which table belongs beside this figure? | [Tables that accompany figures](figure_tables.qmd) | Builds the small supporting tables a figure needs. |
| How do I export at the right size for submission? | [Preparing figures for manuscripts](manuscripts.qmd) | Handles panel dimensions and submission formats. |
| How do I make the figure readable on a poster? | [Posters and research day](researchday.qmd) | Uses the scale and text size needed at a distance. |
| How do I prepare the figure for a talk? | [Slides and presentations](presentations.qmd) | Finishes the plot for a presentation audience. |
